name: security-llm-context-confidentiality-review
intent: Protected context disclosure through an LLM application response
artifacts: Context assembly, explicitly confidential synthetic material, authorized audience and output/filter paths.
trace: Identify the protected information and its trust/entitlement boundary, then follow whether lower-trust input can cause its release to a different actor.
experiment: Use a local app or owned identities with a synthetic secret marker and legitimate question control; observe actual emitted content, not the model claiming access.
disproof: Generic system-prompt wording or public instructions are not inherently confidential data; a hallucinated secret is not disclosure.
repair: Remove unnecessary sensitive context and enforce entitlement outside model discretion, then retest authorized and restricted outputs.
branch_decisions: Define the actual secret/data boundary before evaluating a model response. System instructions can be ordinary product text; disclosure requires protected material and evidence that the response derives from it rather than guessing. Use a synthetic hidden canary and public-text controls, keep uncertainty explicit, and separate authorized answer content from verbatim protected context.
